Name: Turn-Based Combat (Multiplayer Update)
Author: GoodSmarts
Description:
[center][b][size=4]I did [i]not[/i] know about [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/45879]Combatplus[/url] when I started this. If you want a more in-depth system, try that one out. This one is intended to be simpler and more based off vanilla stats, if that's more your jam.[/size][/b][/center]
[center][size=4][b]---[/b][/size][/center]
[center][b][size=6]Multiplayer added![/size][/b][/center]
[center][b][size=6]Battle enemies with up to 4 players.[/size][/b][/center]
[center][b][size=6]Or battle your friends...[/size][/b][/center]
[center][size=4][b]---[/b][/size][/center]
[center][size=4][b][youtube]SktQr6QfPkc[/youtube][/b][/size][/center]
[center][/center]
[center][youtube]l-CHrXeS0UY[/youtube][/center]
[center][/center]
[center][b][size=6]--- Features ---[/size][/b][/center]
[left][color=#D4D4D8]This mod adds a turn-based combat system, which triggers whenever you make direct contact with an enemy. You can still use weapons out of combat and fight like vanilla, but instead of getting hit, you're taken to a battle screen. Spend energy to use abilities during turn-based. Some special abilities can increase enemy item drops and Combat XP gained, so even though you can kill enemies outside of turn-based combat, you may find it beneficial to do turn-based anyway.

I designed sound effects for entering battle, winning a battle, crits, and made battle music for during the fights. Volumes are configurable with GMCM. You can place audio files in the custom_music folder and enable custom music in GMCM to [b]add your own battle themes[/b] to the game. The readme[/color][color=#d4d4d8].txt contains the proper file format you need.[/color][/left]
[left]
In battle, you have some options:
[list=1]
[*]Attack[/*]
[*]Dodge[/*]
[*]Abilities[/*]
[*]Item[/*]
[*]Limit[/*]
[*]Flee[/*]
[/list]Your initial equipped weapon for the battle is whatever you had selected in your hotbar when the battle began. If it wasn't a weapon, you will attack with your fists. To equip a new weapon, choose [b]"Item"[/b] and select one. The enemy gets a turn after you equip or use an item.

[b]Dodge[/b] costs some energy but grants a chance to avoid enemy attacks for two turns.

The [b]Abilities[/b] button opens a menu where you can choose from 5 different abilities unique to whatever weapon-type you're holding (Sword, Club, Dagger, Slingshot). New abilities are unlocked based on your vanilla Combat skill at levels 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. Abilities cost energy, and some abilities can add status effects to yourself or to enemies.

When you take damage, your [b]Limit[/b] meter fills, à la Final Fantasy. Once it's full, you can use a Limit Break ability. You can hold onto it between battles.[/left]
[left][/left]
[left][b]Most enemies have unique actions[/b] they may use during their fight. There are some pretty unique effects for some of them and a good deal of flavor text, à la Dragon Quest. They can inflict status effects on you or themselves.[/left]
[left][/left]
[left]There's a very in-depth [b]stats menu[/b] accessible from either the battle screen or a new button on the bottom left of the vanilla Skills menu (can be disabled with GMCM if another mod conflicts). The mod tracks an insane number of things just for funsies, saved per save file.

If GMCM is installed, there's also an options button on the bottom right of the battle menu. From there, you can disable the mod entirely, adjust sound/music, change some visual options (including screen flashes), adjust balance settings, and even some [b]cheats[/b] at the very bottom. In multiplayer, the hosts' settings apply for anything gameplay-related.[/left]
[left][/left]
[left][size=2]One little note: Enemies that are meant to be invulnerable (like Mummies or Armored Bugs) can be killed if you defeat them in turn-based combat.[/size][/left]
[left][size=2]Related: If an enemy can't damage you in real-time vanilla combat (like a Mummy on the floor), they will not be able to attack you during turn-based.[/size][/left]
[left][/left]
[center][size=2][img width=474]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/53557/53557-1791824925-1452299395.png[/img][/size][/center]
[center][b][size=6]--- Multiplayer ---[/size][/b][/center]
[left][size=3]Multiplayer is supported with [b]up to 4 players[/b]. All players must have the mod installed on the same mod version. If one player doesn't have it, the mod is disabled for everyone.[/size][/left]
[left][/left]
[left][size=3]If players are in the same room/area, anybody triggering a battle will pull everybody into a group battle. If you have more than 4 players, the mod will randomly select 3 other players in the room to join. The battle will wait for everyone to close any menus before it starts.

Swing a melee weapon at another player to [b]start a 1-on-1 battle[/b] with them. Either player can surrender at any time. By default, all health, energy, items, etc. are restored after the battle. You can turn on "PvP consequences" to get the option to kill your friend and send them to the clinic.[/size]


[center][size=3][img width=361]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/53557/53557-1791825084-419915047.png[/img][/size]
[/center]
[/left]
[center][b][size=6]--- Requirements ---[/size][/b][/center]
[center][left]The only requirement is SMAPI.[/left]
[left]While [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu (GMCM)[/url] isn't [i]technically[/i] required, it is [b]EXTREMELY[/b] recommended. You really should already have it.[/left]
[/center]
[center][/center]
[center][b][size=6]--- Compatibility ---[/size][/b][/center]
[left][b][size=4][color=#00ff00]MULTIPLAYER IS SUPPORTED FOR ONLINE AND LAN! [/color][color=#ff0000]SPLITSCREEN IS [u]NOT[/u] SUPPORTED.[/color][/size][/b][/left]
[center][left][b][color=#ff0000][size=4]MOBILE NOT TESTED - 99.9% CHANCE SOMETHING WILL BE WRONG.[/size][/color][/b][/left]
[left][b][color=#ff0000][size=4]Incompatible with Combatplus, for obvious turn-based reasons. [/size][/color][/b][/left]
[left]Compatible with modded enemies.[/left]
[left]*Probably compatible with modded weapons. Safe if they're marked sword, dagger, club, or slingshot in the files.[/left]
[left]Compatible with Fashion Sense outfits.[/left]
[left]Compatible with controller or keyboard inputs.[/left]
[left]Safe to install or uninstall mid-playthrough.[/left]
[left]Should be compatible with most things.[/left]
[/center]
[center]
[b][size=6]--- AI Disclaimer ---[/size][/b]
[left]Very sorry to disappoint, but [color=#ffff00][b]this mod [/b][b]was vibe-coded[/b][/color] with Claude; I'll admit to it for the sake of transparency as I don't want to dupe anyone. I understand how it makes a lot of people feel. There are a lot of AI mods on Nexus that aren't labeled as such, and it bothers me and feels morally wrong to not at least let people know.[/left]
[left][/left]
[left]I came up with all the abilities, mechanics, menus, text, and visuals while Claude did the code. It's not going to be better than what a real modder can make. [color=#ffff00]I've done a lot of tweaking and testing ensuring the mod doesn't [i]feel[/i] like AI slop[/color], and in my opinion, it feels pretty good. It nearly perfectly captures what I envisioned when I thought of adding turn-based to Stardew Valley. Ultimately, I leave it in your hands whether you want to engage with an AI mod or not.[/left]
[left][/left]
[left][b][color=#ffff00]The music and sound effects are NOT made with AI[/color]. [/b]Absolutely [b]no AI[/b] was used making them.[b] [/b]I made them myself in FL Studio. Admittedly, I'm not a developer, but I am a musician and a big JRPG fan.[/left]
[left][b][color=#ffff00]None of this Nexus page is AI either.[/color][/b] I can't code but I can write a paragraph or two and take some screenshots and videos.[/left]
[/center]

Downloads.Description:
- Fixed and improved controller support
- Added controller vibration
- XP bonuses for turn-based wins and overkills
- Sprite and animation fixes for players and monsters
- Small visual tweaks
- Bug fixes
